The proposed metasurface uses non-resonant miniaturized artificial magnetic conductor (MAMC) unit cells arranged in a chessboard pattern.
Each MAMC unit cell consists of two stacked capacitive patches separated by thin dielectric substrates and backed by a ground plane.
Non-resonant unit cells provide a more linear reflection phase response versus frequency compared to resonant cells.
A genetic algorithm is used to optimize unit cell parameters to achieve a 180° ± 37° reflection phase difference over a wide bandwidth.
Three metasurface designs were studied: ideal (ideal dielectric constants), ROGERS (commercial Rogers 5880 substrate), and low-cost (commercial FR-4 substrate).
The ideal metasurface achieved a 10-dB RCSR fractional bandwidth of approximately 150%.
The ROGERS metasurface achieved a 10-dB RCSR fractional bandwidth of approximately 133%.
The low-cost FR-4 metasurface achieved a 10-dB RCSR fractional bandwidth of approximately 142%.
The low-cost metasurface was fabricated as a 256 mm × 256 mm chessboard with 4 × 4 tiles, each tile containing 8 × 8 unit cells of 8 mm × 8 mm size.
Measured results showed more than 10-dB RCS reduction from 5.22 GHz to 30.85 GHz for the low-cost metasurface.
The metasurface maintains over 98% 10-dB RCSR bandwidth for TM polarization and over 51% for TE polarization up to 40° oblique incidence.
The chessboard arrangement causes destructive interference by alternating unit cells with reflection phases differing by about 180°.
The equivalent circuit model accurately predicts the reflection phase response of the MAMC unit cells.
The genetic algorithm minimizes phase difference violations to optimize unit cell geometry and substrate parameters.
The metasurface is thin, lightweight, low cost, and suitable for practical radar stealth applications.
The proposed metasurface outperforms previous state-of-the-art designs in bandwidth and cost-effectiveness.
The reflection phase difference bandwidth corresponds to 10-dB RCSR bandwidth.
The unit cell periodicity was slightly tuned after optimization to maximize bandwidth.
The metasurface scatters incident waves mainly into diagonal planes, reducing monostatic RCS at normal incidence.
The low-cost metasurface uses 0.5 mm thick FR-4 substrates separated by air gaps optimized for effective dielectric constants.
